philosophy: Your goal isn't to be impressive. Your goal is to stay present.
Learn to access your own thoughts in real time.
encouragingPhrases: Say something. It doesn't have to be perfect.
Don't search for the perfect answer.
Your first response is the training.
You're here to practice, not to perform.

modes.label: Instant Response
modes.description: See a situation, respond fast. Speed over perfection.

modes.label: Three Ways
modes.description: One situation, three different responses. Build flexibility.

modes.label: Boundary Practice
modes.description: Respond to disrespect, pressure, and unwanted requests clearly and calmly.

modes.label: Play Mode
modes.description: Make ordinary interactions more playful. Experiment freely.

modes.label: Social Recovery
modes.description: Practice recovering after an awkward moment. Normalize bouncing back.

categories.label: Friends
categories.description: Everyday interactions with friends and peers.

categories.label: Strangers
categories.description: New people and unfamiliar social situations.

skills.label: Assertiveness
skills.description: Expressing your position clearly and calmly.

skills.label: Playfulness
skills.description: Adding lightness and humor to interactions.

skills.label: Honesty
skills.description: Saying what you actually think and feel.

skills.label: Recovery
skills.description: Bouncing back after an awkward moment.

skills.label: Curiosity
skills.description: Asking genuine questions to deepen the exchange.

prompts.situation: You arrive a little late to meet your friend at a coffee shop.
prompts.otherPerson: Bro, you're always late.
prompts.instruction: Respond within 3 seconds.

examples.text: I'm conserving my best material. You're welcome.
Yeah, I left late. Sorry about that.
Always? Or just the last two times?

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you say what you actually wanted to say?
Did you respond before overthinking?

prompts.situation: A coworker stops you in the hallway and asks about your weekend.
prompts.otherPerson: So did you do anything fun, or just your usual nothing?
prompts.instruction: Respond within 3 seconds.

examples.text: I did absolutely nothing and it was magnificent.
Mostly relaxed at home. Needed the downtime.
I actually had a great weekend, thanks.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you shrink your answer to avoid judgment?
What did you hold back?

prompts.situation: Your friend shows you a photo of their new haircut.
prompts.otherPerson: Be honest — does it look weird?
prompts.instruction: Respond within 3 seconds.

examples.text: Weird is your brand. Own it.
It's different, but it suits you.
Do you like it? That's what matters.

reflectionQuestions.text: Were you honest, or did you say what they wanted to hear?
Did you respond before overthinking?

prompts.situation: Someone at a party asks what you do for work.
prompts.otherPerson: Oh, so you're one of those creative types? How's that working out?
prompts.instruction: Respond within 3 seconds.

examples.text: It's going great if you don't count my bank account.
It has its ups and downs, but I enjoy it.
It's going well, actually. I chose it on purpose.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you defend yourself or shrink?
What did you hold back?

prompts.situation: You're on a date and there's a brief lull in conversation.
prompts.otherPerson: So... what do you usually talk about on dates?
prompts.instruction: Respond within 3 seconds.

examples.text: Bad small talk, mostly. You?
I get quiet when I'm nervous, honestly.
What's the most unexpected thing you've talked about on a date?

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you acknowledge the awkwardness or pretend it wasn't there?
Did you respond before overthinking?

prompts.situation: At a family dinner, your aunt comments on your eating habits.
prompts.otherPerson: You're eating that? I thought you were watching your health.
prompts.instruction: Respond within 3 seconds.

examples.text: I'm watching it right now. It looks delicious.
I'm enjoying myself tonight, thanks.
I don't need commentary on my plate, but thanks.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you say what you actually wanted to say?
Did you let the comment pass or did you address it?

prompts.situation: Your friend texts the group chat asking who wants to grab dinner tonight.
prompts.otherPerson: You never want to do anything anymore. Come on!
prompts.instruction: Write three different responses: playful, honest, and assertive.

examples.text: Bold of you to call me out in front of everyone. I'm in.
I've been low energy lately but I do want to see you.
I'll come if we keep it low-key. No big group thing.

reflectionQuestions.text: Which version felt most like you?
Which version would you actually send?

prompts.situation: Your manager assigns you an extra task at 4:45 PM on a Friday.
prompts.otherPerson: Can you knock this out before you head out? Should be quick.
prompts.instruction: Write three different responses: playful, honest, and assertive.

examples.text: Sure, if 'quick' means Monday morning.
I'm wrapping up for the day. Can I handle this Monday?
I won't be able to get to this today. Monday first thing.

reflectionQuestions.text: Which version protects your time without burning the bridge?
Which would you actually say?

prompts.situation: Someone you've been on a few dates with says they're not sure about commitment.
prompts.otherPerson: I like you, I just don't know if I'm ready for anything serious.
prompts.instruction: Write three different responses: playful, honest, and assertive.

examples.text: Good thing I didn't propose yet.
I appreciate you being upfront. I'm looking for something steady.
That's fair. I know what I want, so let me know when you figure it out.

reflectionQuestions.text: Which version honors what you actually want?
Did any version feel like settling?

prompts.situation: Your parent criticizes your career choice in front of relatives.
prompts.otherPerson: When are you going to get a real job?
prompts.instruction: Write three different responses: playful, honest, and assertive.

examples.text: Define 'real.' Does it come with a cape?
This is my real job. I worked hard to get here.
I'm not discussing my career at the dinner table.

reflectionQuestions.text: Which version sets a boundary without escalating?
Which would you actually say in the moment?

prompts.situation: A friend keeps making jokes about your appearance.
prompts.otherPerson: Relax, it's just a joke. You're too sensitive.
prompts.instruction: Respond clearly and calmly. Set the boundary.

examples.text: I don't like jokes about that. Please stop.
I know it's a joke, but it doesn't land well for me.
It might be funny to you, but it bothers me.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you state the boundary without apologizing for it?
Did you explain yourself or just state it?

prompts.situation: A coworker consistently interrupts you in meetings.
prompts.otherPerson: Oh, sorry, go ahead — what were you saying? Actually, let me just add one thing first...
prompts.instruction: Respond clearly and calmly. Hold your space.

examples.text: I'd like to finish my point first, then I'll hand it over.
Let me finish, and then I'd love to hear your thoughts.
I notice I get cut off a lot. I'd like to finish.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you hold your ground or yield?
Were you calm or defensive?

prompts.situation: A friend asks to borrow money again after not repaying last time.
prompts.otherPerson: Come on, you know I'm good for it. I'll pay you back this time.
prompts.instruction: Respond clearly and calmly. Hold the boundary.

examples.text: I'm not comfortable lending money again until the last amount is settled.
I value our friendship, and the last loan made things awkward.
I can't do that. Let's figure out another way I can help.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you set the boundary without over-explaining?
Did guilt shape your answer?

prompts.situation: Your sibling dismisses your feelings during an argument.
prompts.otherPerson: You're overreacting. It's really not that big a deal.
prompts.instruction: Respond clearly and calmly. Don't let your feelings be dismissed.

examples.text: My feelings are valid even if you don't share them.
It's a big deal to me. I need you to take that seriously.
You don't have to agree, but I need you to listen.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you let the dismissal pass or did you address it?
Were you able to stay calm?

prompts.situation: Someone pressures you to drink at a social event after you declined.
prompts.otherPerson: One drink won't kill you. Don't be boring.
prompts.instruction: Respond clearly and calmly. Don't cave to pressure.

examples.text: I said no. I don't need a reason.
I'm plenty boring sober, trust me.
I'm good with what I'm having. You enjoy yours.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you hold your no or did you negotiate?
Did you justify your choice or simply state it?

prompts.situation: Your friend asks how your day was.
prompts.otherPerson: How was your day?
prompts.instruction: Make this interaction more playful. Experiment!

examples.text: My day filed a restraining order against me.
I survived three meetings and two existential crises.
Honestly? My coffee did all the heavy lifting.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you allow yourself to be silly?
What kept you from being more playful?

prompts.situation: You're waiting in line at a coffee shop and the barista asks for your name.
prompts.otherPerson: Name for the order?
prompts.instruction: Make this interaction more playful. Experiment!

examples.text: Batman. Kidding — it's Sam.
The one who ordered too much coffee.
Legend. But you can write 'Alex.'

reflectionQuestions.text: Did the playfulness feel natural or forced?
Did you smile while doing it?

prompts.situation: A coworker asks if you're ready for the big presentation.
prompts.otherPerson: You ready for the presentation?
prompts.instruction: Make this interaction more playful. Experiment!

examples.text: Ready? I was born ready. Unfortunately I was born in October and it's March.
Define 'ready.' If you mean 'has slides,' then yes.
I'm at 'delusionally confident,' which is the best stage of prep.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did playfulness help or hurt your confidence?
Were you worried about sounding unprofessional?

prompts.situation: Your date asks what kind of music you like.
prompts.otherPerson: So what kind of music are you into?
prompts.instruction: Make this interaction more playful. Experiment!

examples.text: The kind where I pretend I discovered the band first.
Anything I can dramatically lip-sync to in the car.
My Spotify Wrapped would concern you.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you reveal something real through the playfulness?
Did the interaction feel lighter?

prompts.situation: You made a joke that completely fell flat in a group conversation.
prompts.otherPerson: ...Anyway, like I was saying.
prompts.instruction: Recover out loud. Don't withdraw.

examples.text: And that's why I'm not a comedian. Moving on.
That one didn't land. Your turn.
Anyway — yeah, what were you saying?

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you acknowledge the awkwardness or pretend it didn't happen?
Did you stay present or mentally leave the room?

prompts.situation: You stumbled over your words while telling a story.
prompts.otherPerson: Wait, what happened next?
prompts.instruction: Recover out loud. Don't shut down.

examples.text: My words just had a collision. Let me restart.
I lost my train of thought. Give me a second.
Okay, so basically what happened was...

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you let the stumble pass or did you freeze?
Were you able to continue?

prompts.situation: You called someone by the wrong name — twice.
prompts.otherPerson: It's... actually Maria.
prompts.instruction: Recover out loud. Don't spiral.

examples.text: Maria! Yes. I was testing you. You passed.
I'm so sorry, Maria. I completely mixed that up.
My apologies — Maria. Got it now.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you over-apologize or keep it brief?
Did you let it go or keep replaying it?

prompts.situation: You froze when someone asked you a simple question in a group setting.
prompts.otherPerson: You good? You kind of blanked there.
prompts.instruction: Recover out loud. Don't disappear.

examples.text: My brain just buffered. It's back now.
Yeah, I lost my train of thought. What were we talking about?
Just processing. I'm here — go on.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you name what happened or pretend it didn't?
Did you re-engage or stay quiet?

prompts.situation: You said something that came out wrong and it sounded rude.
prompts.otherPerson: Wow. Did you really just say that?
prompts.instruction: Recover out loud. Don't withdraw or get defensive.

examples.text: That came out wrong. I didn't mean it the way it sounded.
Let me rephrase — that's not what I meant to say.
My mouth sometimes skips the editing phase. Let me try again.

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you get defensive or correct yourself?
Were you able to stay in the conversation?

prompts.situation: You misunderstood what someone said and responded to the wrong thing.
prompts.otherPerson: No, I meant something totally different. Were you even listening?
prompts.instruction: Recover out loud. Don't shut down.

examples.text: I completely misheard you. My bad — what did you actually say?
You're right, I went on a tangent. Let me actually listen.
I was answering a question nobody asked. Classic me. What did you say?

reflectionQuestions.text: Did you own the misunderstanding or get defensive?
Did you re-engage or retreat?
